text:
kai: heads-up — bringing up helios14b-int4 in canary (rack-b). seeing slow-start behavior and intermittent OOMs when we hit small bursts of concurrent short chats.
model-deploy-bot: canary deploy started on node-7; image=helios14b:int4-rc3; pool=canary; cfg=default-prefetch.
sara: noticed KV cache growth after ~25–40k tokens on the same session, memory fragmentation looks suspicious (free lists not compacting).
matt: do we have the batch/window settings and max_new_tokens for that canary? our recent defaults were 128 but some of these models prefer smaller max_new_tokens.
kai: current canary config snippet:```json
{"batch_ms":50,"max_batch_tokens":4096,"max_new_tokens":128,"prefetch":true,"kv_warmup":true}```
olga: try disabling aggressive kv_warmup and reduce prefetch concurrency. that often helps with frag on int4 backends. also drop batch_ms to 20 for low-latency use.
matt: agreed — set max_new_tokens=64 for canary, batch_ms=20, and enable adaptive batching (seq-aware). also add KV eviction TTL of 30s for canary traffic. :thumbsup:
sara: applying changes now:```bash
redwoodctl canary update --model helios14b --set max_new_tokens=64 --set batch_ms=20 --set kv_eviction_ttl=30s --set prefetch=false
``` will watch metrics for 30m.
kai: redeployed. initial smoke looks better latency-wise but GPU memory still creeps during an 8-concurrency synthetic spike. attaching small log excerpt:```
[2026-03-20T12:11:05Z] INFO request=start seq_len=12 concurrency=8 gpu_mem=10.2GB kv_live=1.2GB
[2026-03-20T12:11:05Z] INFO request=start seq_len=512 concurrency=8 gpu_mem=11.8GB kv_live=1.9GB
[2026-03-20T12:11:06Z] ERROR oom killed process pid=4234
```
olga: if GPU mem still climbs under concurrency, try trimming KV cache between requests for this canary (`kv_trim_on_evict=true`) before we touch allocator settings. that avoids large arena fragmentation.
matt: alternative: short-term jemalloc purge on worker loop, long-term prefer KV eviction + smaller per-request KV prefetch window. also consider reducing max_batch_tokens for canary to limit worst-case temporary memory spikes.
sara: added dashboard panels: kv_live_bytes, kv_evictions/sec, batch_wait_ms, batch_size_hist. also wired an alert for gpu_mem>total*0.85 for canary nodes. will post updates if we see regression.
kai: running the synthetic harness Oli suggested:```bash
./eval_harness --model=helios14b --quant=int4 --concurrency=8 --prompt-set=short-chat --max_new_tokens=64 --seq_len=1024 --duration=5m
``` will report perf numbers in ~6m.
matt: if we still see fragmentation after these config tweaks, I can try a quick runtime build that disables continuous prefetch and enforces synchronous kv eviction to validate hypothesis. low-risk canary build only.
sara: after 15m the canary looks stable: no OOMs in last 10m, kv_live peaked lower and auto-evicted. leaving canary running with new defaults for another 24h before wider rollout. thanks team. :party_parrot:
